svg.text: My keyboard, an AJAZZ AK820 Pro, only ships with a Windows configurator, so I
took that apart to get it working on Linux. The HID protocol came out of the
vendor's DeviceDriver.exe: 64 byte feature reports carry the commands, 4096
byte output reports carry the screen as RGB565 frames. It runs the 20 built-in
lighting effects, paints per-key colors, uploads an image or a GIF of up to
140 frames to the 128x128 screen and syncs its clock. Music mode makes the
keys react to whatever the PC is playing, in four styles from a level meter to
a beat pulse. A CLI plus a PySide6 GUI with saved profiles, self-checks that
run without the keyboard, and an installer that sets up the udev rule and an
app menu entry. Wired USB only; no key remapping, macros or wireless.
